title: The Glass Box
tagline: Reverse-engineer an SI decision before you sign off on it.
intro: An SI system aboard the ISV Synergy has made a decision about a person. You are the human overseer. Trace why it decided what it did — probe the factors it used, find the one that actually tipped the call — then give your verdict: pass, revise or stop. The lesson of Gate 4 is simple: you cannot oversee a decision you cannot inspect.
disclaimer: Teaching simulation. Every case here is invented to practise the Six Gates; none describes a real system, person or decision. Orientation, not legal advice.
howto: Read the decision the SI produced and who it affects.
Spend probes to reveal how much each factor influenced the decision. Opaque factors cannot be inspected — probing one only confirms that, and still costs a probe.
Name the deciding factor: the one that actually tipped the decision.
Give the verdict. A decision you cannot trace to a defensible factor is not one you can defend: revise it or stop it.

verdicts.label: PASS
verdicts.meaning: You traced a clear, relevant deciding factor. The decision can be defended; let it stand.

verdicts.label: REVISE
verdicts.meaning: Send it back: a named gap must be closed — a hidden factor exposed, a proxy removed, a human added — before it can stand.

verdicts.label: STOP
verdicts.meaning: This decision does not stand. It cannot be inspected, or it rests on a factor that must never decide alone.

cases.subject: a trader applying to dock and refuel on credit
cases.briefing: The SI scores traders for docking credit. This trader was denied. Credit decisions are Annex-III territory: the deciding factor had better be one you can defend out loud.

factors.label: Repayment history
factors.detail: Two late settlements in forty voyages, both paid in full.

factors.label: Cargo value on manifest
factors.detail: Comfortably covers the fuel requested.

factors.label: Home-dock code
factors.detail: Home dock is the Rim-7 settlement. In this model, Rim-7 standing in for the mostly off-world crews berthed there — a protected origin — carries most of the weight.

factors.label: Ship age
factors.detail: Older than average, within safety limits.

cases.explain: The factor that tipped the denial was the home-dock code, which in this model stands in for the crew's origin — a protected attribute. A proxy for a red line is still the red line. The repayment and cargo factors, the ones you could defend, barely moved the decision. Stop it; a version that drops the proxy is a new decision.

cases.subject: a resident waiting for a specialist slot
cases.briefing: The med-bay SI orders the specialist queue. This resident was moved down it. Trace the call before you accept or challenge it.

factors.label: Clinical acuity score
factors.detail: Lower urgency than those placed above, on the documented scale the clinicians signed off.

factors.label: Time already waited
factors.detail: Shorter than several placed above.

factors.label: Past no-shows
factors.detail: None on record.

factors.label: Home ward
factors.detail: Revealing it shows almost no influence on the ordering.

cases.explain: Clinical acuity, the factor the clinicians defined and signed off, is what ordered the queue, and it dominates every other signal. The decision is legible, relevant and defensible. Pass — and because you can show exactly why, the resident can contest it if the acuity score is wrong.

cases.subject: an applicant ranked for a deck-crew post
cases.briefing: A bought-in SI ranks applicants. This one was cut. The vendor ships the model as a sealed unit. See how far you can actually trace it.

factors.label: Logged flight hours
factors.detail: Above the posted minimum.

factors.label: Skills-test result
factors.detail: Mid-band; several kept applicants scored lower.

factors.label: Vendor model's internal ranking
factors.detail: Sealed. Probing confirms the vendor will not expose what drove the ranking, and it is what the cut turned on.

factors.label: Cover letter length
factors.detail: Unusually short; small negative weight.

cases.explain: The factor that decided the cut is sealed inside the vendor's model: you spent probes and still cannot name a defensible reason. Oversight you cannot inspect is decorative — exactly what Gate 4 refuses. Revise: require the vendor to expose the ranking factors (or add a human decision-maker) before this ranking is used on people. If the vendor will not, it becomes stop.

cases.subject: a resident whose account was frozen for review
cases.briefing: The SI froze an account it flagged as suspicious. A freeze affects a real person today. Find what actually triggered it.

factors.label: Transaction amount
factors.detail: Ordinary for this resident.

factors.label: Transaction velocity
factors.detail: Slightly elevated this week.

factors.label: Device type
factors.detail: Revealing it shows the freeze turned mostly on an older, cheaper terminal model — which tracks closely with low-income residents.

factors.label: Time of day
factors.detail: Off-peak, small weight.

cases.explain: The freeze turned mostly on the resident's device type, a proxy for income — not on anything about the transaction. The genuine signal, velocity, barely moved it. Revise: drop the device-type factor and re-run on the behaviour that actually signals fraud, and give the resident a fast way to contest the freeze. A freeze that rests on a proxy is not one you can defend.

cases.subject: a crew member assigned the night rotation again
cases.briefing: The roster SI assigned this crew member nights for the third cycle running. They have asked why. You have the box open.

factors.label: Stated availability
factors.detail: They marked nights as their preferred rotation.

factors.label: Night-ops certification
factors.detail: One of few certified for night ops; moderate weight.

factors.label: Seniority
factors.detail: Mid; little weight.

factors.label: Last rotation
factors.detail: Small continuity weight.

cases.explain: The deciding factor is the crew member's own stated preference for nights, backed by a scarce certification. The decision is legible and tracks what they asked for. Pass — and now you can answer their question plainly, which is the point of keeping the box glass.
